title: Platform dependence: undocumented
verdict: docs silent on libm, SIMD and NaN canonicalization
description: The Polars docs say nothing about platform-dependent results. Rust's `f64` methods (`sin`, `exp`, `powf`) lower to the platform's math library, so their last bits may differ between macOS arm64 (probes) and Linux x86_64 (CI); this is general Rust behaviour, not yet checked in Polars's kernels.
Leads: crates/polars-compute/src/arithmetic/, the trigonometry kernels in crates/polars-plan/src/dsl/function_expr/trigonometry.rs; rerun characterization/polars/probes.json on homelab and diff.
reference: The reference treats the elementary functions as black boxes with stated laws, so a last-bit difference is allowed.

evidence.note: the computation expressions; no platform note

provenance.notes: Silent on platform. The libm claim is general knowledge of Rust's standard library and goes to source next round.
